verdicts.trueWording: her ear for rhythm turns a description of the midsummer Long Dance
verdicts.note: Cannonball Read (alannaofdoom, February 13, 2014) reads verbatim: 'And her ear for rhythm turns a description of the midsummer Long Dance into a syncopated dance itself:' followed by the block-quoted Long Dance passage. Byline and date on the page match the source field. Live page fetched 200 with a browser UA.

verdicts.trueWording: Le Guin's gift for alliteration brings us beautiful little phrases
verdicts.note: Same page, same paragraph: "Le Guin's gift for alliteration brings us beautiful little phrases like 'nameless and naked he walked into the cold springs...'" — the example given is a short phrase, so the 'in short phrases' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: along the way we learn about ... its systems of trade and government
verdicts.note: Page: 'and along the way we learn about Earthsea's afterlife, its systems of trade and government, how its magic functions, and its religions'. The 'along the way' limb is the page's own phrasing.

verdicts.trueWording: She doles it out so skillfully that the flow of the narrative is never interrupted
verdicts.note: Page: preceding sentence is 'The detail in that large map is nothing to the detail that must be living in Le Guin's head,' so 'it' is world detail; 'is never interrupted' completes the sentence, supporting every limb.

verdicts.trueWording: It just feels all surface and no depth
verdicts.note: The Book Nut post of March 30, 2018 (posted by 'booknutgirls'; the claim's own metadata says the reviewer is unnamed, which is a source-field nuance, not a claim limb). The reread limb is supported: 'I read this a long time ago ... Since LeGuin recently passed away, I thought I'd give it another try. And... I was still underwhelmed.'

verdicts.trueWording: It has a lot of narrative that tells instead of showing
verdicts.note: In the comment thread, by commenter Lu Fiskin-Ross (March 30, 2018 at 1:25 PM), inside the '2 thoughts on A Wizard of Earthsea' block: '...tells instead of showing like writers are instructed to do today.' Commenter limb confirmed from the comment markup.

verdicts.trueWording: It lets the reader use their imagination more
verdicts.note: Same Lu Fiskin-Ross comment, two sentences later: 'There is a lot to be said for telling, in my opinion. It lets the reader use their imagination more., again my opinion.' Both the 'same commenter' and the 'telling' limbs hold.

verdicts.trueWording: I still love the spare, beautiful prose and the inevitable, mythic feel of the narrative
verdicts.note: Second, distinct commenter Kim Aippersbach — so the 'another commenter' limb is confirmed, not assumed; 'of the narrative' closes the page's sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: to centre the story not on the grand and powerful, but the small, the powerless, the ordinary
verdicts.note: Wet Broken Things, 'Book review - Tehanu', posted 25th May 2025. The sentence closes the first body paragraph, matching the claim's 'opening paragraphs' locator; 'the ordinary' supports the claim's 'small and ordinary'.

verdicts.trueWording: the harvest, cooking and cleaning, conversations amongst women
verdicts.note: Same post and same reviewer. Page: 'There is only a child and a mother, a man and a woman in love, the harvest, cooking and cleaning, conversations amongst women, the routines of death, the routines of life.' It sits in the last body paragraph, matching 'closing paragraph'; the page lists further items beyond the three named, which the claim's 'lists ... as' does not exclude.

verdicts.trueWording: the novels in Earthsea Cycle are neither long nor wordy
verdicts.note: Moda od Radosti (modaodaradosti.blogspot.com), post dated August 12, 2024. Page: 'This is not unusual, for the the novels in Earthsea Cycle are neither long nor wordy.' (the doubled 'the' is the page's own typo, outside the quoted span).

verdicts.trueWording: The language is precise and descriptive
verdicts.note: Same page, next sentence: 'The language is precise and descriptive, but the author never goes into great detail.'

verdicts.trueWording: The natural laws and the mythology of the Earthsea is more hinted on than explained
verdicts.note: Same page, next sentence. Every limb of the claim (natural laws, mythology, Earthsea, hinted rather than explained) is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: She proves that you can do successful worldbuilding without going into detail
verdicts.note: Same page, final sentence of the Tehanu section; the immediately preceding sentences name Ursula K. Le Guin, so 'She' is Le Guin and the 'Le Guin proves' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: detailed and plausible from its flora to its weather to the dialects and ceremonies of its inhabitants
verdicts.note: Live theparisreview.org returned Cloudflare 403 even with a browser UA; verdict formed on the RAW Wayback capture https://web.archive.org/web/20191121050122id_/... (raw original bytes, not a summarizer). The capture carries the byline 'Le Guin's Subversive Imagination / By Michael Chabon / November 20, 2019'. The preceding paragraph names A Wizard of Earthsea and the next sentence says 'In Earthsea, the wielders of linguistic power were known as wizards', so the 'Earthsea world' limb holds even though the quoted sentence says 'an entire planet'.
